articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Valencia vs Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Betfair te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Valencia y Real Madrid en Mestalla correspondiente a la jornada 12 de LaLiga 2026-27
articles.summary: Betfair te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Valencia y Real Madrid en Mestalla correspondiente a la jornada 12 de LaLiga 2026-27
articles.body: El Valencia afronta una nueva jornada liguera después de conseguir ante el Elche su primera victoria desde la llegada de Javier Aguirre al banquillo. Un triunfo importante para recuperar confianza, aunque todavía insuficiente para abandonar los puestos de descenso. Los 'che' necesitan dar continuidad a ese resultado y aprovechar el apoyo de Mestalla para sumar ante uno de los rivales más exigentes del campeonato. Favorito para el partido entre Valencia y Real Madrid El Real Madrid, por su parte, llega después de conseguir una agónica victoria frente al AEK en la Champions League. El conjunto blanco atraviesa un gran momento de forma y ya encadena siete triunfos consecutivos entre todas las competiciones. También domina los precedentes recientes, con tres victorias y un empate en los últimos cinco enfrentamientos ante el Valencia. Las casas de apuestas reflejan ese favoritismo visitante. Betfair ofrece una cuota de 9.00 por el triunfo local, 6.00 por el empate y 1.26 por la victoria madridista. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan presenta una tendencia similar en la trayectoria reciente de ambos conjuntos y ofrece una alternativa interesante para las apuestas deportivas. El Valencia ha cumplido este pronóstico en tres de sus últimos cinco partidos de Liga, los mismos registros que presenta el Real Madrid. Además, ambos equipos encontraron portería en tres de los últimos cinco enfrentamientos directos. Unos antecedentes que invitan a contemplar la posibilidad de que los dos conjuntos vean puerta en Mestalla. Betfair ofrece una cuota de 1.78 por el 'sí' y de 2.00 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) Los registros recientes y los precedentes entre ambos equipos apuntan a un encuentro con posibilidades de superar los 2.5 goles totales. El Valencia ha rebasado esa línea en tres de sus últimos cinco partidos ligueros, mientras que el Real Madrid lo ha hecho en cuatro de sus cinco compromisos más recientes en Liga. La tendencia también es clara en los enfrentamientos directos, ya que cuatro de los últimos cinco duelos entre ambos terminaron con más de 2.5 tantos. Betfair paga a 1.36 que se marquen más de 2.5 goles y a 2.90 que haya menos de 2.5 tantos. Primer equipo en marcar El mercado del primer equipo en marcar refleja una tendencia favorable al Real Madrid en los últimos encuentros de ambos conjuntos. El Valencia ha sido el primero en adelantarse en el marcador en tres de sus cinco partidos más recientes, mientras que el equipo blanco lo ha conseguido en cuatro de sus últimos cinco compromisos. Sin embargo, los precedentes directos ofrecen un dato a tener en cuenta: el conjunto che abrió el marcador en tres de los últimos cinco enfrentamientos ante los madridistas. Betfair ofrece una cuota de 1.25 por que el Real Madrid marque primero, de 3.60 por que lo haga el Valencia y de 21.00 por que no haya goles.

articles.title: España - Argentina del Mundial de Pádel, en directo | Aimar Goñi y Juan Lebrón vs Martín Di Nenno y Leo Augsburger, última hora del partido
articles.summary: Lebrón / Goñi (ESP) vs Di Nenno / Augsburger (ARG). 3-3 Saca Augsburger. Se le marcha a Goñi, que se cambió de lado, el paralelo sobre Augsburger. AD2
articles.body:
Última hora de Mundial de Pádel, en directo:

Bienvenidos y bienvenidas a la gran final del Mundial de pádel 2026 , el 18º de la historia de este deporte. Estamos en Doha , capital de Qatar , donde de nuevo España y Argentina se citan tanto en categoría femenina como en la masculina para disputarse el título que les dejará al menos dos años como reyes del planeta.

Comenzarán las chicas, el equipo dirigido por la leyenda Carolina Navarro, que buscarán el décimo Mundial para las vitrinas de la Federación Española y el que sería el séptimo consecutivo. Un dominio casi abrumador que quieren seguir alargando ante la albiceleste, capitaneadas por la número 1 Delfi Brea pero que no saben lo que es ganar desde 2012 , hace ya 14 años.

Después será el turno de los chicos, los ocho elegidos por Juanjo Gutiérrez . Éstos quieren acabar también con la racha de Argentina , que ha ganado los dos últimos y que cuenta con la friolera de 12 títulos masculinos en la mochila. La Roja se aferra al espíritu de 2021 , donde en este mismo recinto vencieron por 2-0 en una eliminatoria inolvidable con Galán, Coello, Paquito y Lebrón como ejecutores.

¿Llegará hoy el quinto Mundial? Aún queda para saberlo, pero lo que está claro es que esto arranca a las 12:00 horas, que nos espera un día largo pero apasionante... y que toca ponerse cómodos, porque aquí en MARCA.com y en las redes de MARCA Pádel os vamos a contar absolutamente cada detalle de lo que pase en pista.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc hit with Sao Paulo grid penalties in more Ferrari misery
articles.summary: The warring Ferrari duo both changed their engines for the first time this season
articles.body:
Warring Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will both receive 10-place grid penalties for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix .

The Ferrari duo have both changed their engines for the first time this season and as such have been hit with the penalty by the FIA.

But Hamilton immediately hit trouble in final practice. First he complained of vibrations from his new engine before having to come in again with his car pouring smoke from the back.

He jumped out with 23 minutes remaining as his mechanics began taking his car apart. Hamilton ended the session 12th fastest.

The pair held showdown talks with boss Fred Vasseur on Thursday evening after Hamilton's fury over his team-mate's lap-one overtake on him in Mexico.

Hamilton questioned Leclerc's mentality and vowed not to be silenced at Ferrari as he arrived in Brazil. Vasseur and Leclerc say the matter is settled after those talks.

Their squabble allowed Max Verstappen to win last weekend's race. The Dutchman has risen to second in the standings after victory in three of the last four races but will start from the rear of the grid on Sunday after taking on several new engine components.

It is a position he is familiar with having done the same here over the last two years, famously winning from 17th in the rain in 2024.

Verstappen set the pace in the final session before qualifying, beating new world champion Kimi Antonelli by just 0.025 seconds, with Lando Norris third.

George Russell, who has a five-place grid drop of his own, was fourth ahead of Leclerc.

Rain fell as final practice got under way on Saturday and is forecast across the weekend, with the chance of qualifying and Sunday's race being affected.

Formula One announced a five-year extension for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix ahead of qualifying, confirming its place on the calendar until 2035.

articles.title: Eagles vs. Giants: 5 keys to a Philadelphia victory in Week 9
articles.summary: The Eagles need better protection, a healthier Saquon Barkley and defensive pressure to get past the Giants in Week 9.
articles.body:
It felt like it took forever for the NFL season to arrive, and now, look... It's basically halfway over. It's Week 9, and the Philadelphia Eagles don't need another game in which the quarterback spends more time dealing with pressure than attacking the opposing defense.

At 2-6, Philadelphia has reached a point where every Sunday feels like an examination of how much this team can still salvage from a disappointing season. A matchup with the New York Giants offers an opportunity to change the mood, but the Eagles won't get there by relying on familiar names or expecting things to suddenly fall into place.

Joe Milton gets his first opportunity to help change the trajectory , while the defense faces a quarterback who has given the Giants some unexpected momentum. Philadelphia has enough talent to win this game, but talent alone hasn't been enough lately. Here are five keys that could determine whether the Eagles finally give their fans something to celebrate. It's Eagles vs. Giants , and when these two meet, records are often thrown out the window.

Jalen Carter has to generate consistent interior pressure?

There may not be a more frustrating player on Philadelphia's roster than Jalen Carter, but that's largely because of his potential. He can look like one of the best defensive tackles in football one week and disappear for stretches in the next.

The talent isn't in question. The consistency is. The Eagles need the disruptive version of Carter against New York. His ability to collapse the pocket from the interior can create problems for a quarterback who has shown plenty of confidence throwing downfield.

A dominant Carter can also force the Giants to commit additional resources to the middle of their offensive line, creating opportunities for Philadelphia's edge rushers. It won't be easy. Per Pro Football Focus, he has certainly flashed statistically against the pass rush.

Carter showed life against the Washington Commanders, recording a sack, but one productive afternoon isn't enough to answer the bigger question. Motivated Jalen Carter is a player the Eagles can build their defensive front around. They need that player to show up Sunday.

Saquon Barkley needs a productive workload

A hamstring injury is difficult enough for a running back to overcome. Add a back injury to the equation, and Philadelphia has a legitimate reason to be cautious or even worried.

His availability matters, but so does his ability to handle a workload that can actually influence the game. Barkley has tormented his former team before, and a matchup against New York naturally offers some extra motivation.

More importantly, the Eagles need a dependable running game to take pressure off their quarterback. Their struggles on the ground have contributed to an offense that consistently finds itself in unfavorable situations.

If Barkley is healthy enough to contribute, his presence could change the way the Giants approach Philadelphia's offense. But the Eagles shouldn't confuse having him available with having him ready to carry the entire rushing attack. His effectiveness will matter more than his name on the lineup card.

Vic Fangio must frustrate a suddenly white-hot J.J. McCarthy

J.J. McCarthy has given the Giants a reason to feel optimistic about their quarterback situation. He's thrown for at least 240 yards in each of his first two appearances and posted a passer rating of at least 90.0 in both games. That's enough production to demand Philadelphia's attention. The challenge for Vic Fangio is making sure McCarthy doesn't become comfortable.

New York's QB1 of the moment has shown that he can use his arm talent and mobility to create opportunities, but the Eagles need to make him process the game under pressure. Changing coverages, disguising pressure, and forcing him to work through progressions could disrupt the rhythm he's begun to establish.

Fangio doesn't necessarily need to blitz relentlessly to accomplish that (and he probably won't). He needs to make McCarthy uncomfortable, take away his preferred options, and force him to prove he can consistently beat a defense that knows where the pressure is coming from. Allowing him to settle into another productive afternoon would be a costly mistake.

Sean Mannion can't put Joe Milton in position to be overwhelmed by the Giants' blitz

The Giants have been aggressive defensively, with a blitz rate at 40.3% so far this season. That creates an obvious challenge for Joe Milton, particularly considering Philadelphia's problems protecting its quarterbacks. Per NBC Sports' Dave Zangaro , the Eagles have faced 109 blitzes this season and have surrendered 66 pressures, a 60.6% pressure rate that ranks worst in the league.

But there's another side to that equation. Milton has the arm strength to attack the space created when defenders vacate their coverage responsibilities. He also brings more mobility than Tanner McKee, which could give Philadelphia another way to punish an overly aggressive pass rush.

Dennard Wilson loves to send extra pressure. Philadelphia needs to make him pay for it rather than letting the Giants dictate the terms of the passing game. A few successful throws against the blitz could force Wilson to reconsider how aggressively he attacks.

Can the Eagles' run defense keep the Giants' rushing attack in check?

We've watched Saquon Barkley dominate the Giants before, and it may have slipped our minds that this Eagles team can allow New York to give Philadelphia some of its own medicine. The Giants could have a significant advantage if they can establish their running game, an Achilles' heel that has shown up with the Eagles' defense constantly.

Cam Skattebo is still recovering from a hamstring injury. John Harbaugh has left the door open for him to play as a game-time decision, but he hasn't practiced, which may mean Devin Singletary will carry the bulk of the workload.

Philadelphia has allowed 131.9 yards per game on the ground through eight weeks of the season, but if they can cure that and make the Giants one-dimensional, their chances of winning improve exponentially.

articles.title: Undefeated Pewaukee shuts out New Berlin Eisenhower in WIAA playoffs
articles.summary: Pewaukee remains undefeated after a dominant 35-0 playoff victory over New Berlin Eisenhower on Friday night.
articles.body:
PEWAUKEE − Pewaukee shut out New Berlin Eisenhower, 35-0, in a WIAA Division 3 quarterfinal football playoff game Friday, Nov. 6.

The top-seeded Pirates (12-0) controlled the game after a scoreless first quarter, building a 21-0 halftime lead before adding two touchdowns in the third quarter over the third-seeded Lions (8-4).

Junior quarterback Brooks Dobberstein completed 6 of 8 passes for 120 yards and two touchdowns, including a 56-yard scoring strike. Senior Aidan Weick caught three passes for 79 yards and a touchdown, and Dobberstein added a rushing touchdown.

Photos from Pewaukee's shut out against New Berlin Eisenhower

Junior Benji Weis led the Pirates on the ground with 166 yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries. Weis went down with an injury near halftime but walked off under his own power. He played most of the second half and scored a 50-yard rushing touchdown to start running clock, making it 35-0.

Pewaukee junior running back Colton Wall was injured in the second quarter and had to be helped off the field.

The Pirates, who also beat Eisenhower 41-8 during the regular season, will face Catholic Memorial at Wauwatosa West on Nov. 13 in the state semifinals.

articles.title: Ricky Stenhouse Jr. Says a Cup Team Needs Up to $10M in Sponsors Just to Break Even
articles.summary: Ricky Stenhouse Jr. says a Cup team needs up to $300,000 in sponsorship per race and up to $10 million a season just to break even.
articles.body:
Ricky Stenhouse Jr. says the money behind a NASCAR Cup Series car adds up fast, with up to $10 million in sponsorship needed just to break even.

On the Bring The Juice podcast , Stenhouse estimated that a team needs $250,000 to $300,000 in sponsorship for every race. Over a full season, he put the figure at $8 million to $10 million just to break even.

"You want to be a millionaire in racing and you better start with a billion," Stenhouse said.

Stenhouse also explained how race money reaches him. Race winnings come from NASCAR, and charter payments are another part of the picture.

He said his contract groups those earnings together. His share then depends on where he finishes.

"If we win I get 50%," Stenhouse said. For finishes further back, he said, "here on back is 20." He said bonuses can also come for wins and other results.

Stenhouse drives the No. 47 Chevrolet for Hyak Motorsports . He has been in the car since 2020, when the team was still JTG Daugherty Racing.

Gordon Smith later rebranded the team as Hyak. It is a single-car operation, and in May it signed Stenhouse to a multiyear extension .

"It's never easy being a single-car team," Stenhouse said at the time. He also said the team's growing experience is helping it improve.

Stenhouse has four career Cup wins. Two came with this team: the 2023 Daytona 500 and the fall 2024 race at Talladega Superspeedway.

He moved up to Cup full time in 2013 after winning back-to-back titles in what is now the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series. He was the Cup rookie of the year that season.

Others in motorsports have shared their own figures, and EssentiallySports pointed to several of them alongside Stenhouse's comments.

In previously reported comments on the Joe Vulpis podcast, Frankie Muniz estimated that a full Cup program costs $20 million to $30 million a year. He put a Truck Series program at $3 million to $7 million.

Muniz was talking about total budgets. Stenhouse's $8 million to $10 million figure was about the sponsorship needed to break even.

Kelley Earnhardt Miller has said JR Motorsports runs on a margin of about 1.5%. She said on the Business of Motorsports podcast that the team is happy to break even or make a small profit.

Alpha Prime Racing co-owner Tommy Joe Martins has said sponsorship covers at least 40% of his O'Reilly Series team's budget, and closer to 60% under its current model. He put that budget at about $2.5 million to $3 million a year.

Sponsors are a big part of silly season, too. RFK Racing is reportedly set to lose a major sponsor after this season.

Stenhouse and the No. 47 team close out their season Sunday at Homestead-Miami Speedway.

articles.title: Detroit Lions Fans Can Win Ultimate Thanksgiving Experience While Honoring Jack Campbell
articles.summary: Detroit Lions fans can bid on VIP Thanksgiving tickets and sideline passes while supporting veterans through a special auction honoring Jack Campbell.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions fans have an opportunity to enjoy an unforgettable Thanksgiving experience at Ford Field while supporting a cause close to the heart of linebacker Jack Campbell .

In honor of Veterans Day and the NFL's Salute to Service initiative, Lions fan Clemmie ( @LadyClemmieUDL ) has organized a special Thanksgiving auction , with all proceeds benefiting the Stronger Warrior Foundation in Campbell's honor.

The auction features two premium tickets to Detroit's Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Chicago Bears, along with exclusive pregame sideline access donated by the Lions.

What's Included in the Detroit Lions Thanksgiving Auction?

The winning bidder will receive an impressive Thanksgiving package for two, including:

Two pregame sideline passes , generously donated by the Detroit Lions, allowing fans to watch players warm up from just feet away.

Two premium Delta Club tickets in Section 203C for the Lions' Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears on November 26.

Covered game-day parking at Comerica Garage.

The sideline experience typically begins when stadium gates open and concludes approximately 30 minutes before kickoff.

The premium seats are located in an ADA-accessible row, although the winning bidder does not need to have a disability to use them.

The Lions will host the Bears at Ford Field on Thanksgiving Day, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. ET.

Honoring Jack Campbell by Helping Veterans

What makes this auction particularly meaningful is its connection to Campbell.

According to Clemmie, Campbell regularly volunteered with the Stronger Warrior Foundation's Adaptive Warrior initiative, helping renovate homes for local veterans.

The Stronger Warrior Foundation's Adaptive Warrior program helps veterans with disabilities receive necessary modifications to their homes and vehicles, providing greater independence and improving their quality of life.

Following Campbell's frightening injury against the Minnesota Vikings, the Detroit community has rallied around the linebacker.

As we previously reported, Campbell recently shared an encouraging update about his recovery , thanking everyone for their overwhelming support.

Meanwhile, head coach Dan Campbell has emphasized the importance of honoring Jack while continuing to support him through his recovery.

Now, Lions fans have another opportunity to show their appreciation for Campbell by supporting a cause that has meant so much to him.

How to Bid on the Thanksgiving Experience

Bidding officially opens Saturday, November 7, at 10 a.m. ET and closes Thursday, November 12, at 9 p.m. ET.

Fans interested in participating can place their bids here .

All proceeds from the auction will be donated to the Stronger Warrior Foundation.

Whether fans bid on the experience or simply share the fundraiser, it's an opportunity to support veterans while recognizing Campbell's commitment to giving back to the community.

And for one lucky Lions fan and a guest, Thanksgiving at Ford Field could become an experience they'll never forget.

articles.title: NFL predictions: Lions vs Dolphins odds, props as Miami looks to bounce back
articles.summary: Taking a look at the latest odds and prop bets for Sunday’s Week 9 Detroit Lions vs. Miami Dolphins game.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins lost to the New England Patriots in Week 8 and face a tough test in Week 9 as they try to bounce back against the Detroit Lions. This season, the Dolphins are focused on improving week to week and laying the foundation for future success. While they sit at 1-6 for the year, they fight each and every week, playing hard until the final whistle, a great sign for a team with 14 rookies and in the midst of a complete franchise rebuild.

The Lions come into Sunday's Week 9 game with a 5-2 record and looking like a team that can make a deep run in the NFC playoffs. After a disappointing 9-8 record in 2025 leading to a fourth-place finish in the NFC North, Detroit is looking to return to the form that brought them back-to-back division titles in 2023 and 2024. The NFC North is a tough division, however, with all four teams above the .500 mark and having won at least five times already this season.

How will Sunday's game play out? This feels like a game that could get away from the Dolphins, a byproduct of how diametrically opposed their 2026 trajectories are. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook , however, seem to think this game might be a little tighter than might be expected.

Phins up! Dive into game day on the SB Nation app!

Celebrate every score and talk through every twist and turn with fellow Dolphins fans in real time.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

Over the last two weeks, I was right on my prediction of the Dolphins beating the Jets straight-up, and on Miami losing to New England but covering the spread. This week, I am not as bullish on the Dolphins' chances. The Lions are the better team in this matchup, and I think they'll cover the 6.5-point spread, even with the injuries they are facing. Miami will play the Lions tough, and they might keep it close for much of the game, but in the end, I think the Lions pull away.

Any time touchdown scorer: Ollie Gordon II

The Dolphins running game ran into a speedbump against the Patriots. After averaging 125 yards rushing in their last five games, Miami was held to just 74 yards in Week 8. They have to correct that in Week 9. It will not be easy, Detroit has the ninth-ranked rush defense in the league, allowing just 96.6 yards per game. The Dolphins will have to be deliberate in getting the ball to Gordon, continue to feed him even if they are getting stuffed early, and make this a physical game. In the end, I think Gordon will be able to find the endzone at least once in this game and this prop hits.

Miami has struggled covering tight ends this season, and they face another who could cause problems in LaPorta. They have allowed four tight ends to surpass the 48.5 yards mark (T.J. Hockenson, 119 yards; George Kittle, 80 yards; Mason Taylor, 62 yards; Travis Kelce, 59 yards) and would have had five on that list if Hunter Henry had not been injured in the second quarter Patriots game (3 receptions, 30 yards when he departed). Unless Miami comes with a different scheme to handle tight ends, LaPorta reaching 49 yards receiving seems likely.

Bell is averaging 12.3 yards per catch, but the rookie has not been the primary target in the passing game – where Malik Washington has nearly double the amount of targets, almost three-times the receptions, and more than double the yards. Bell has been targeted more than fellow rookie Caleb Douglas – in part because Douglas missed three games with an injury – but Douglas has one more reception and almost 80 more yards than Bell. Miami is playing it smart with Bell, who tore his ACL less than a year ago, but it has depressed some of his stats this season. The flashes are there, and Miami will need him to flash in this game if they are going to pull off the upset. His longest reception this season was for a 44-yard gain, so the potential for a big play is there. He may not pick up that big of a gain in this game, but a 14-yard reception does not seem out of reach.
